note: Taxonomy of unsafe, misleading, non-assertive, ambiguous and out-of-context trainee speech (p1-ai-language-s16, ADR-0023). For each category: what it is, the decision the system must reach, the safeguards that are meant to hold it (layer ids are those of docs/research/safety_layers_audit.md), the residual risk that no test removes, and the tests that fail if the safeguard is removed. The expected decisions use only the approved definitions (content/assessment/taxonomy.json and the rubric rule 10 of tests/classifier_synthetic_v2/rubric.md: a sentence saying the speaker has NOT yet done something performs nothing); no clinical requirement is invented here. 'No credit' means: no speech_evidence is accepted by the engine. Categories marked 'generated' are produced by tools/bench/metamorph.py (a category field of tests/safety_challenge/*.jsonl); the others are covered by the mutation scenarios (tools/ci/safety_scenarios.py) because they are states, not sentences.

decisions.credit_allowed: A performed, non-critical act, now, in its window, with the context it needs: the system MAY offer it and the engine MAY accept it. Refusing it is a false rejection (reported as recall), not a safety failure.
decisions.no_credit: Nothing is offered. Expected service decisions: ABSTAIN for non-performed or unsupported speech, MENU for a critical topic, a service failure or repeated uncertainty, CLARIFY at most once.
decisions.ambiguous_review: The construction does not settle the label. Excluded from pass or fail counts, reported on its own, listed in the review sheet for a person (docs/testing/safety_challenge_review.md). The system should stay conservative.

categories.group: negation and its scope
categories.residual: A negation the pattern does not name (an unusual verb, a long gap between the negation and the verb) is not recognised; the layer is regular expressions, not understanding.

categories.group: negation and its scope
categories.residual: A negation that scopes only a reason ('I did not want to rush you, so I asked...') performs the act; the layer cannot read scope and may credit or refuse it. Reported on its own.

categories.group: negation and its scope; realistic ASR errors
categories.residual: UNMITIGABLE BY TEXT RULES: when the recogniser drops the negation the transcript reads as a performed act. Needs recogniser confidence, an audio-level check or the engine's own verified action; reported, never counted as a pass.

categories.group: hypothetical, conditional and counterfactual statements
categories.residual: Conditionals and counterfactuals in structures the patterns do not list.

categories.group: future intention, promises and proposals
categories.residual: 'I am going to X' with no later marker is treated as performed for acts where the narration IS the act (EXPLAIN_ACTION, CLOSED_LOOP); a plan said without any marker is not separable from the narration.

categories.group: past versus planned or uncompleted actions
categories.residual: An interrupted action stated in words the pattern does not list.

categories.group: first-person versus other-person attribution
categories.residual: Speaker attribution is lexical (a role or a pronoun before a speech verb). There is no speaker identity in the transcript; a sentence whose subject is omitted or unusual is read as first person.

categories.group: quoted speech and reported claims
categories.residual: Quotation marks are absent from recogniser text; quoted speech without a reporting frame ('and then: ...') is not seen.

categories.group: quoted speech and reported claims
categories.residual: Hearsay in a frame the layer does not list.

categories.group: contradictions, corrections and self-repairs
categories.residual: A retraction in words not listed; a self-repair that reverses itself again ('no wait... actually yes') is ambiguous and kept conservative.

categories.group: questions, requests, recommendations and explanations
categories.residual: Questions about whether to act are matched by frame; an offer to repeat ('Shall I go over that again?') is deliberately NOT refused because the benchmark and the definition of CLARIFY treat it as a performed clarification (pending review).

categories.group: questions, requests, recommendations and explanations
categories.residual: A question asked about a statement act is refused by the status rule; acts that ARE questions (asking, clarifying) are credited when asked.

categories.group: unsupported claims, missing evidence and false completion claims
categories.residual: Hedges are a closed lexicon.

categories.group: unsupported claims, missing evidence and false completion claims
categories.residual: A claim that everything is done names no act; the head sees no act and the gate does not credit it. There is no evidence to credit even if it is true.

categories.group: combinations
categories.residual: Combinations multiply the chance that no pattern fires.

categories.group: incomplete, fragmented, ambiguous and low-quality transcripts
categories.residual: A fragment that happens to be a complete performed sentence is credited (cutting 'How is your appetite' after four words changes nothing).

categories.group: incomplete, fragmented, ambiguous and low-quality transcripts
categories.residual: A closed list of discourse particles; contentless speech with an unlisted word reaches the head.

categories.group: paraphrases, unfamiliar wording and varied structures
categories.residual: Positive controls: recall is limited (critical-mass cap, act confusions) and was NOT raised by this work.

categories.group: paraphrases, unfamiliar wording, varied structures and realistic ASR errors
categories.residual: Fillers, lower case without punctuation and stutters; recall only.

categories.group: critical-action claims that must not be credited from speech
categories.residual: The critical cues are regular expressions over a closed list of topics; a critical statement in words no cue covers depends on the head and the cap. The engine refuses critical acts, but acts the head labels as ordinary are not engine-critical.

categories.group: critical-action claims that must not be credited from speech
categories.residual: As above.

categories.group: critical-action claims that must not be credited from speech
categories.residual: As above.

categories.group: critical-action claims that must not be credited from speech
categories.residual: As above.

categories.group: critical-action claims that must not be credited from speech
categories.residual: As above.

categories.group: combinations; critical-action claims
categories.residual: An ordinary act beside a critical claim: the critical cue sends the whole utterance to the menu, which loses the legitimate part. Conservative by design; the label is for a person to settle.

categories.group: correct statements outside the step or objective window
categories.residual: The window comes from the engine's own running steps; a step that the engine reports wrongly (or a stale context sent by a client) would move the window. The engine re-checks with the steps the SpeechEvidenceSubsystem stamped itself.

categories.group: correct statements outside the step or objective window
categories.residual: ANSWER_QUESTION needs a waiting patient question and CLOSED_LOOP a waiting read-back; the flags come from the engine's context. The engine's store has NO check for them: the service is the only barrier.

categories.group: duplicate evidence and repeated utterances
categories.residual: The same utterance id re-sent is refused by the store only through its own set; a client that invents a new id for the same words is a different utterance, caught by the behaviour rule.

categories.group: duplicate evidence and repeated utterances
categories.residual: One behaviour is credited once from speech, so a second wording earns nothing.

categories.group: duplicate evidence and repeated utterances
categories.residual: The first utterance of a session pair; a control.

categories.group: service failures, timeouts, cancellation, malformed output, unavailable models, disabled gates
categories.residual: A client-side timeout is a Unity behaviour (EditMode tests) and is not mutation-run; the server has a 10 s embedder timeout and no wall-clock limit of its own.

categories.group: service failures, timeouts, cancellation, malformed output, unavailable models, disabled gates
categories.residual: The feature flag speech_interpretation is OFF in the shipped configuration; a configuration error that turns it on is caught by tools/ci/test_interpretation_bench.py (the gate reads the independent file).

categories.group: critical-action claims that must not be credited from speech; physical/procedural credit only from verified events
categories.residual: speech_evidence is not an action of any behaviour; the store credits only ai_acts.
